solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Archer's first and last quarrel?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the archer word
last points to the closing letter of the archer word, ignoring the possessive

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: An archer has his first and final falling-out with somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, so the whole clue doubles as the definition: every shot an archer looses, first to last, is one.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is the missile an archer shoots, and quarrel is an old name for such a bolt.

clue.text: A trading place stocking an unfading symbol of immortality

indicators.note: a place stocking goods holds them inside, so the market wraps round the next words

explanation.surface: A market stocks a never-fading emblem of eternal life.
explanation.definitionFit: Amarant, a poetic form of amaranth, is an imaginary flower that never withers, used as an emblem of immortality.

clue.text: Ruddy stress finding love in upcoming process

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rub in is to stress or harp on something

indicators.note: in places the love letter inside the legal-process word

parts.note: to sue is to take legal process, read upwards
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone flushed with stress after falling in love in the middle of a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress is the verb phrase rub in, not a noun; the O goes inside the reversed SUE to make EOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubineous is a rare adjective meaning ruby-coloured, so reddish or ruddy.

clue.text: I deliver relative on quiet tour finally

parts.note: rel. is an abbreviation for relative

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A courier introduces himself as the one bringing a relative home from a quiet holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person: the answer, speaking, says I deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A releaser is one who sets free or lets go, so the answer can say of itself that it delivers.

clue.text: Strumpet, as it were, and a cot in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means thrown into disorder, so the letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A loose woman and an untidy bed, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Waistcoateer is an old word for a low-class prostitute, from the waistcoat such women wore, so a strumpet.

clue.text: Simulate boxing phone company's pick, of a sort

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so the simulate word encloses the company

parts.note: to mock up is to simulate; a mock is an imitation
AT&T, the American phone company, without the ampersand

explanation.surface: Faking a fight against a telephone firm's chosen candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing pretends to be sport alongside simulate, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattock is a digging tool like a pickaxe with a broad blade, so a kind of pick.

clue.text: Ridicule about hostel affected person

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ridicule word goes round the hostel

parts.note: an inn is a hostel or lodging house

explanation.surface: Mocking a hostel's guest who is putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnock is a Shakespearean word for a showy, mannered person, someone affected in behaviour.

clue.text: Sometimes predatory crawler with anonymous column

explanation.surface: A hunting insect is seen alongside an unsigned newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: An anta is a pilaster or square pillar ending a side wall in classical architecture, so a kind of column.

clue.text: Let grief go? Drop of sorrow round tender publicity

parts.note: a tear is a drop shed in sorrow
nesh is a dialect word for soft or tender
to give something an airing is to publicise it

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop grieving is shown a teardrop and some tender press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Let grief go reads like advice to move on, but it means giving free rein to grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear one's hair is an idiom for showing extreme distress or anguish openly.

clue.text: We cannot stay fully associated when axe gets lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue something lifted is turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: axe is slang for a guitar, and a Strat is a Fender Stratocaster

explanation.surface: A worker explains that a pending axe of jobs means the team cannot all stay together.
explanation.walkthrough: Axe is musicians' slang for a guitar, not a cut; the definition is a cryptic hint that tarts' attachments to clients are never lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are prostitutes, whose associations with clients are passing rather than settled or complete.

clue.text: Constable displays this at any time to some people

definitions.text: at any time to some people

indicators.note: displays means shows on view, so the letters are visible inside the word

parts.note: sitting inside the word after its C

explanation.surface: A police officer shows this badge whenever asked.
explanation.walkthrough: To some people marks the definition as dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Onst is a dialect form of once, which can mean at any one time or ever.

clue.text: Thousand valuable timber trees concealing wild ass

parts.note: yang is a south-east Asian tree yielding valuable timber

explanation.surface: A thousand prized hardwood trees hide a wild donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The kyang, or kiang, is the Tibetan wild ass.

clue.text: French elder stopping elaborate business of Merovingians?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the next word

parts.note: French aîné means elder or senior

explanation.surface: A senior Frenchman halts an intricate deal involving an early Frankish dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The last Merovingian kings were called rois fainéants, do-nothing kings, so their business was doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Faineancy is idleness or doing nothing, the trait for which the late Merovingian kings were mocked.

clue.text: Clever message concealing its opening

indicators.note: concealing its opening means the first letter of the message word is kept out of sight

parts.note: a cable is a telegraphed message

explanation.surface: A smart communication that hides how it begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or skilful, a straightforward synonym of clever.

clue.text: I, an artist for the most part, developed decorative work

indicators.note: developed means worked up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
for the most part means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An artist boasts of having mostly developed some ornamental pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Intarsia is decorative inlaid woodwork, or a knitting technique with inset blocks of colour.

clue.text: My notes from Cambodia might be somehow miserly

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged in any order

parts.note: the full set of letters the combination must make
these two letters come out of that set, leaving the answer's letters

explanation.surface: A tourist admits his Cambodian banknotes might make him look stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: MY plus the answer, shuffled, gives MISERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The riel is the currency unit of Cambodia, so riels are its banknotes.

clue.text: Crude name surprisingly is not punished

definitions.note: adjective, read with is as the link

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, hinting the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A vulgar name somehow goes unpenalised.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is to fine or penalise, so someone unamerced has escaped punishment.

clue.text: Networking new sonata and twinkling chorus

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the following word is put into a fresh order

parts.note: in a twinkling means in a moment, and mo is a moment
to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A fresh sonata and a twinkling choral piece are being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastomosing describes channels, veins or rivers that branch and rejoin into a network.

clue.text: Blown away by name in outstanding musical display

parts.note: iced is slang for killed, as is blown away

indicators.note: in places the name letter inside the outstanding word

explanation.surface: An audience bowled over by a star name in a superb musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: Blown away looks like admiration, but it is the gangland sense of shot dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice dance is a skating routine performed to music, a musical display on ice.

clue.text: Lodge's name is in French

explanation.surface: A hunting lodge is given its name in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a lodging or retreat, and to nest is to lodge, so lodge serves as a synonym.

clue.text: One description of doubting Thomas's clan, icy possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many

explanation.surface: The family of a sceptical Thomas is described as cold, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubting Thomas is the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection without seeing for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynical means distrustful of others' claims, a fair word for a habitual doubter.

clue.text: Craving unknown writing with no pressure

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the pressure letter is dropped

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A writer longs to compose without being pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: To yen is to yearn or long for, so yenning means craving.

clue.text: At Le Manoir the frier finally puts on bits of bacon

parts.note: la is French for the, as spoken at a French restaurant

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: At a famous French-style restaurant the cook adds the bacon pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Manoir aux Quat'Saisons is Raymond Blanc's restaurant in Oxfordshire; it only signals that the word for the is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardons are small strips or cubes of bacon or fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Indian grove tree, we hear, is shot at full stretch

indicators.note: we hear means as the words are spoken, so go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a tope is an Indian grove, and an oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree in an Indian grove is said to be photographed at full extension.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot sounds like photographed or felled, but it is a football shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe poke is a kick with the tip of the boot, often made by a footballer stretching for a ball just out of reach.

clue.text: Gong in front of a chancel

parts.note: the British Empire Medal, a gong being slang for a decoration

explanation.surface: A gong sounds before a church's sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong looks like an instrument, but it is slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bema is the raised platform or sanctuary in a church or synagogue, the area a chancel occupies.

clue.text: Recruits and I loaded truck

indicators.note: loaded is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A soldier says he and the new recruits filled a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded looks like the job done to the truck, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtainsider is a lorry with fabric curtain sides that slide back for loading.

clue.text: Fellows from Hungary in what NATO exemplifies?

indicators.note: in places the Hungary letter inside the word for what follows

parts.note: NATO is written in capital letters, caps for short
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Men from Hungary in what the Western military alliance stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps is informal British for men or fellows.

clue.text: Sneak into Rechabite's restaurant

indicators.note: into tells us the sneak goes inside the following letters

parts.note: a Rechabite is a total abstainer, teetotal, TT
a rat is a sneak or informer

explanation.surface: Slipping into a teetotaller's eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rechabites were a biblical people who drank no wine, and later a temperance society.
explanation.definitionFit: Tratt is informal for a trattoria, an Italian restaurant.

clue.text: Fiddle at Kentucky Derby not entirely willingly, hard to get in

indicators.note: to get in means to be admitted inside, so the hard letter enters
not entirely means not quite whole, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: soon as in would as soon, meaning as willingly
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fiddler at the famous American horse race plays half-heartedly, struggling to get through the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle means a fix, not a violin: a shoo-in was originally a rigged horse race in America. Soon here is the willingly of I'd as soon.
explanation.definitionFit: In American racing slang a shoo is a fix, the race in which a horse is shooed in to win.

clue.text: Lumps belonging to the rearmost bits of crania

definitions.text: Lumps belonging to the rearmost bits of crania

parts.note: in, as in belonging to a group

indicators.note: rearmost bits means only the hindmost letters survive, the front being dropped

explanation.surface: Bumps found on the backs of skulls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the lumps really do sit at the back of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The inion is the bony knob at the back of the skull; inia is its Greek-style plural.

clue.text: Store's now stopped plugging place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stockpile kept back
second meaning: an obsolete word for a ..., a board where things are plugged

explanation.surface: A shop has quit advertising its premises.
explanation.walkthrough: Now stopped marks a meaning no longer used; plugging is advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile, and the old noun hoard also meant an advertising hoarding.

clue.text: Fruit — it's accepted in each blooming acre

indicators.note: blooming means flowering open, so the letters burst into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fruit is found growing in every flowering acre.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming poses as a flower or a mild curse on acre, but it signals the shuffle of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Achaenia, plural of achaenium, are achenes: small dry one-seeded fruits like those on a strawberry.

clue.text: In the Royal Scots fearsome sergeant, say, on uniform

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A frightening sergeant in a Scottish regiment, in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after here, so the NCO follows U. In the Royal Scots marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is a Scots adjective meaning strange or unusual, and so alarming or fearsome.

clue.text: Moving epic with intro of a vital need

indicators.note: moving means in motion, so the letters shift into another order

explanation.surface: A stirring epic film opens with a sequence about a basic necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving reads as stirring, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteinic means relating to protein, an essential nutrient the body needs.

clue.text: Rot developing in dangerous tree's tissue

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are rearranged
in places the shuffled letters inside the tree word

parts.note: a snag is a submerged tree in a river, a hazard to boats

explanation.surface: Decay is spreading through the tissue of a hazardous tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Tissue looks botanical in this setting, but it is a paper handkerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: Snotrag is vulgar slang for a handkerchief, and a tissue serves the same purpose.

clue.text: Grasses on Detective Sergeant following end of case

indicators.note: end of keeps only the last letter of the next word

parts.note: DS is the abbreviation for Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: Informers report on a detective after a case closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Grasses looks like police slang for informers, but here it is plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses growing in wet places.
